artworks.title: Couronnement de Voltaire (The Crowning of Voltaire)
artworks.artist: Charles-Etienne Gaucher after Jean-Michel Moreau
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an architectural scene with columns and arches, high ceilings, tiered balconies, and figures engaged in various activities. The drawing features ornate balconies, a central elevated platform beneath a large stone archway, and intricate engravings. The background shows additional arches and structures typical of classical architectural design.

artworks.title: Couronnement de Voltaire (The Crowning of Voltaire)
artworks.artist: Charles-Etienne Gaucher after Jean-Michel Moreau
artworks.medium: etching and engraving on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical scene titled "Couronnement de Voltaire." The image shows a group of elegantly dressed figures gathered around a central bust or statue in an opulent and classical architectural setting. The setting features grand archways and multi-tiered balconies filled with an audience. The figures are dressed in elaborate costumes reminiscent of 18th-century fashion, and appear to be in a celebratory or ceremonious pose. The scene suggests an event in a grand theater or similar venue, with an audience observing from various levels. The image focuses on the details of the architecture and the costuming of the figures.

artworks.title: On y court plus d'un danger
artworks.artist: Louis Germain and Charles Emmanuel Patas after Louis Gabriel Moreau
artworks.description: The image shows a woman on a swing pushed by a man, with a small dog nearby. Trees with detailed foliage surround the scene. The background is a lush forest. The artwork is created using fine-lined brushstrokes, capturing textures and details. The color palette is monochromatic, mainly browns and tans. Light and shadow are used to enhance the detailed rendering.

artworks.title: Le villageois entreprenant
artworks.artist: Louis Germain and Charles Emmanuel Patas after Louis Gabriel Moreau
artworks.description: The image shows a man and a woman seated in a dense forest. The artwork depicts intricate lines and cross-hatching to create texture in the trees and characters' clothing. The color palette is monochromatic, using shades of brown and sepia. The scene is enveloped by thick trees in the background.

artworks.title: Le desir de plaire
artworks.artist: Louis de Surugue de Surgis after Jean-Baptiste Joseph Pater
artworks.description: The image shows a group of women in an indoor scene. The central figure is seated at a table while the others attend to her. The women are elegantly dressed in dresses with intricate details. Their hairstyles are ornate. Some women are standing, attending to tasks, while others are seated. Items on the table include a mirror. In the background, there is a large framed painting and a hearth with candlesticks. The setting reflects the refinement and elegance of an 18th-century interior.

artworks.title: Les plaisir de l'ete
artworks.artist: Louis de Surugue de Surgis after Jean-Baptiste Joseph Pater
artworks.description: The image shows a group of women in an opulent room. A woman is seated on the edge of a bathtub, partially covered by a cloth, while another woman stands beside her, offering a towel. Other women in elaborate gowns are present, with one kneeling and another reaching into a box. One woman is holding a towel, and another is closing a curtain. The background features a decorated wall panel, a large window with curtains, a tiled floor, and a small basin.

artworks.title: La jarretière
artworks.artist: François Marie Isidore Queverdo
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an opulently decorated interior. The composition shows a richly furnished room with ornate drapery and detailed furniture in a Neoclassical style. The scene is framed within an embellished, circular border that includes floral motifs and intricate patterns. The overall aesthetic suggests attention to luxurious fabrics, textures, and decorative elements prevalent during the Rococo period. The intricacy and fine lines of the drawing highlight elaborate patterns on textiles and the elegant design of the interior space.

artworks.title: L'indiscret
artworks.artist: François Marie Isidore Queverdo
artworks.description: The image shows a man and two women interacting. One woman, on the right, faces slightly towards the viewer. She has a delicate profile, elaborate updo, and ornate dress. The man, on the left, faces the woman and wears knee-length breeches and a detailed coat. The second woman is partially hidden behind the first one, facing the man. Both women have updo hairstyles and elegant garments. They are holding the edges of the man's coat. The background is an ornate interior with curtains, a carpet, and an upholstered chair visible. The scene is framed within a round border with garlands and classical motifs.

artworks.title: Nouvelles du bien-aimè
artworks.artist: François Marie Isidore Queverdo
artworks.description: The image shows a seated woman on an ornate sofa, with her body turned slightly to the side and legs partially visible, with one leg raised. Her hair is styled in an elaborate updo, and she has delicate facial features. She is dressed in a flowing garment that drapes over her shoulders and legs. Across from her, another woman is kneeling on the floor, with her upper body turned towards the seated woman. This second woman has voluminous hair styled away from her face and wears a full-length dress with puffed sleeves and a fitted bodice. Both women seem to be interacting closely. The setting is richly decorated, with heavy drapery curtains hanging in the background, enclosing the scene. There is also an ornate side table with a pitcher and a glass next to the kneeling woman. The entire scene is framed by a circular border adorned with a leaf motif, and the background outside of this circular frame is plain and textural.

artworks.title: Nouvelles du bien-aime
artworks.artist: François Marie Isidore Queverdo and Antoine Louis Romanet
artworks.description: The image shows two women in a cozy, intimate setting. One woman is sitting on a bed, partially reclining, with her legs elegantly crossed and draped in a loose, flowing gown that exposes her shoulders. Her hair is styled up. The other woman is seated closely, leaning forward with an attentive posture. She has long hair cascading down and is clothed in a detailed, long-sleeved dress. She appears to be engaged in conversation with the reclining woman. The setting is adorned with luxurious drapery and a side table with an ornate pitcher. The background is rich in fabrics and textures. The scene is within an oval frame, part of a larger artwork with intricate designs and embedded text elements.

artworks.title: Le sommeil interrompu
artworks.artist: Jean Dambrun after François Marie Isidore Queverdo
artworks.description: The image shows a woman lying on a luxurious bed inside a circular frame decorated with flowers and leaves. The woman is reclining against plush pillows with covers partially draped over her body. Her eyes are closed or downcast and she has long, flowing hair. She is wearing a loose-fitting gown that reveals her breast. Beside the bed, a man is partially hidden by heavy curtains, looking at the woman. There is a table with flowers and a decorative object next to the bed. The background is framed by the grand bed curtains.

artworks.title: Au moins soyez discret (At Least Be Discreet!)
artworks.artist: Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a woman from the waist up. She is seated and facing her right, with her left hand raised delicately near her face. Her facial features include a profile with a slightly upturned nose and full lips. Her hair is curly or wavy and adorned with an elaborate cap or headpiece with frills. She is dressed in an ornate, flowing gown with lace and ribbon details, a low neckline, and ruffled sleeves. In the background, there is a decorative wall and a small table with a vase of flowers.

artworks.title: Comptez sur mes sermens (You May Count on Me!)
artworks.artist: Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image displays a bust-length portrait of a person facing a three-quarter view with their head slightly turned to the side and their right hand near their lips. The individual has a refined facial structure with a high forehead, defined features, and hair styled in voluminous curls typical of the 18th century. They wear elegant attire, including a fitted coat with ornate buttons, a waistcoat, and a cravat tied at the neck. A floral decoration is pinned to their chest. The person is framed within an oval, with a curtain and part of a window in the background, implying an indoor setting. The background has subtle shading and prints.

artworks.title: Louise Emilie Baronne de ***
artworks.artist: Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image features a portrait of a woman in profile, shown from the waist up. She is looking to her right, with an elongated nose, prominent forehead, and deep-set eyes. Her hairstyle is typical of the 18th century, with elaborate curls and volume. She is dressed in a formal attire with a lace-adorned plunging neckline. The oval frame includes decorative elements like a floral arrangement, a quiver of arrows, and a bow. The background within the frame has a textured pattern, resembling an engraved print. Below the portrait, there is a decorative plaque with French text.

artworks.title: Adrienne Sophie Marquise de ***
artworks.artist: Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a woman in profile from the waist up. She is positioned to the left, looking into the distance. She has delicate facial features, a straight nose, and full lips. Her hair is styled in curls and she wears an elaborate hat decorated with lace and ribbons. She wears a detailed gown with lace trim and patterns on the sleeves and neckline, and a drop earring is visible. The portrait is in an ornate oval frame with ribbon and floral decorations. Below the portrait is a plaque with text, and the background is textured with fine lines.

artworks.title: Derniere heure de la Baronne de Rebecque
artworks.artist: Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image shows a woman's face and part of her upper body enclosed in an oval frame. She is depicted in a relaxed, slightly reclined position, with her head slightly tilted to the side. She has delicate facial features, almond-shaped eyes, and a serene expression. Her hair is partially covered. She is wearing a voluminous, ruffled cloth wrapped around her head and upper body, adorned with intricate detailing and texture. The background is a plain, textured surface that complements the circular framed design, emphasizing the woman's detailed clothing and facial expression.

artworks.title: Le bal pare
artworks.artist: Antoine-Jean Duclos after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: Drawing of an opulent ballroom scene with chandeliers and figures engaged in dance and conversation. The interior is decorated with chandeliers, wall moldings, curtains, and a detailed floor pattern. The figures wear elaborate costumes typical of a formal ball. The scene conveys luxury and grandeur, capturing a ballroom setting's elegance and social vibrancy.

artworks.title: Le bal pare
artworks.artist: Antoine-Jean Duclos after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate ballroom scene. The image depicts an opulent interior with finely detailed walls adorned with classical motifs and large draped windows. Several grand chandeliers hang from the ornate ceiling, illuminating the room with soft candlelight. The floor is filled with elaborately dressed figures, all wearing period clothing that suggests an 18th-century setting. The central figures are engaged in a dance. surrounding them are onlookers seated or standing, talking amongst themselves or watching the dancers. The scene conveys an air of elegance and refinement, reflecting the social activities and formal gatherings of the time.

artworks.title: Le concert
artworks.artist: Antoine-Jean Duclos after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a grand salon setting with elegantly dressed figures. The detailed interior scene shows an ornately decorated room with drapery-covered windows, elaborate wall moldings, and strategically placed busts and statues. A group of individuals in period attire is seen conversing or admiring a central activity, possibly involving music, as suggested by the presence of musical instruments and music sheets. Intricate details fill the room, capturing an opulent social gathering from the 18th century. The style is classical with attention to textures, patterns, and architectural elements like the ceiling fresco and columned walls.

artworks.title: Le concert
artworks.artist: Antoine-Jean Duclos after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image shows a grand salon scene with a large gathering of people in 18th-century attire. Men and women are seated and standing in an ornate room with high ceilings, decorative moldings, large windows, and a checkered floor. Columns, pilasters, paintings and architectural details adorn the walls.

artworks.title: Le concert
artworks.artist: Antoine-Jean Duclos after Augustin de Saint-Aubin

artworks.title: The First Come Best Served
artworks.artist: Antoine-François Sergent after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.medium: etching and wash manner printed in brown on laid paper
artworks.description: The image shows a woman seated on a bed, with disheveled sheets. Her body is turned to the side as she looks down towards her chest, resting her head against her hand. She wears a long, light-colored dress with loose sleeves. There are a few indistinct figures lying down around her, and a small cat sits by her feet. In the foreground, a man in a hat peeks into the scene from an open door, looking surprised. The background shows a shadowy room with drapery around the bed. The lighting emphasizes the soft, intimate atmosphere of the setting. Below the scene, the words "The first Come first served" are inscribed.

artworks.title: The Place to the First Occupier
artworks.artist: Antoine-François Sergent after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.medium: etching and wash manner printed in brown on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an interior scene within a rustic setting. The image shows a cluttered room with various objects scattered around. In the lower section of the circle, figures are depicted sitting or reclining among objects like wooden boards, a basket, ropes, and textiles. Details in the room include everyday objects such as a bottle, hats, shoes, and a sketching board leaning against a chair. The light source appears indirect, casting soft shadows and highlighting the textures of draped fabrics. A window on the left shows an outdoor view framed by a lattice pattern. A central focus is created by the circle format of the drawing, emphasizing the cozy yet chaotic environment. A ceiling beam in the upper part of the drawing is adorned with what could be a small animal resting or sleeping. The setting conveys casual disarray and intimacy.

artworks.title: La promenade des remparts de Paris
artworks.artist: Pierre-Francois Courtois after Augustin de Saint-Aubin
artworks.description: The image shows an outdoor social scene viewed from a slightly elevated perspective. The horizon is low, with the tops of trees and a row of buildings in the distance. The visual elements include elegantly dressed figures engaged in various activities like walking, conversing, or attending to children. The brushstrokes, done using an etching technique, are detailed and precise, capturing the attire and tree textures. The color palette is a monochromatic sepia tone, giving a timeless quality to the scene. Trees on both sides frame the gathering, creating depth and leading the eye towards the more distant architecture where more people can be seen.
